holds.reason: Turn-prohibition and lane-control signs on physical page forty-five are image-only in the extraction. Their symbols and messages are not established from text; visual evidence and an authorized learner-media disposition are required.

The Yield-sign pedestrian condition begins on physical page forty-four and continues on forty-five. The precise crosswalk wait-until-crossed instruction needs a permitted multi-page source disposition before a one-page fact can claim the whole condition.

The bicycle-lane guidance ends mid-sentence on physical page fifty-nine and continues onto the next mapped section. The unfinished instruction is not completed from memory; a policy-compliant full source span is needed.

The opening bicycle straight-through instruction continues from physical page fifty-nine. The full antecedent and movement condition are not forced into a single-page fact; the complete cross-page disposition remains open.

The interchange route diagrams have not been rendered or cleared for learner spatial-recognition media. Only the explicitly written route instructions are represented; no image-based route is invented.

The maximum-speed paragraph describes a range for other locations without identifying an unambiguous road category or a single default value. That passage is not converted into a guessed universal limit; official clarification is required.

Physical page sixty-nine describes turning left onto a one-way street without the origin condition, while page seventy-three specifies a one-way origin and destination. Only the narrower explicit case is authored; broader origin eligibility remains unresolved.

The left-lane/right-lane movement paragraph on physical page seventy-three is tied to an unreviewed diagram. Its unspecified junction layout is not generalized into permission to turn left from any right lane; visual/layout evidence remains required.

The parking paragraph on physical page eighty attaches an only-if-left-running parenthesis to setting the parking brake. The modifier's intended application is unclear and is not converted into advice to omit a parking brake when the engine is off; issuer clarification is required.

Physical page eighty-one includes hill-parking illustrations. Text supports the wheel-turn directions below, but wheel contact and any rolling sequence shown in the image have not been visually reviewed; no sequence is inferred from the phrase away and against the curb.
The disability-parking symbol on physical page eighty-two is image content not semantically reviewed. Textual eligibility and reserved-space use are covered; visual recognition remains unresolved.

The instruction to wait for a sufficiently large gap after stopping on a short acceleration lane spans physical pages eighty-four and eighty-five. The current one-page fact binding cannot represent that complete conditional instruction without losing its interference qualifier; retain the complete span as coverage debt.

Physical page eighty-seven gives five seconds or one hundred feet for starting from a curb, entering a parking space or changing lanes without resolving which measure applies in each context. Other accepted source sections provide maneuver-specific timing. The procedure is covered, but this unqualified alternative is not taught as a universal timing rule; scope needs reconciliation.

The concluding side-scanning instruction continues from physical page eighty-nine onto ninety with a warning that other drivers may run a light. The local complete side-scanning instruction is covered; the complete cross-page sentence and its rationale remain a binding-span debt.

The blind-spot illustration referenced on physical page ninety has not received semantic visual review. The text definition and shoulder-check rule are source-bound; graphic interpretation remains unresolved.

Physical page ninety-two describes a texting infraction, a hands-free exception, no points, a fine and a commercial-only moving-violation classification. Present legal scope and consequences are not independently established in this frozen-handbook pass. Withhold those legal classifications and any broad hands-free permission until exact current official legal authority is reconciled.

The children-near-roadway instruction on physical page ninety-six continues onto ninety-seven with its unexpected-entry qualifier. Nearby complete child-safety instructions are covered; this complete cross-page instruction remains unresolved under the one-page fact binding.

The horse-passing instruction spans physical pages ninety-seven and ninety-eight. Approaching-rider slowing, no horn and control-difficulty response have local support, but the complete passing-room instruction needs a supported multi-page fact binding.

The bicycle straight-through red-light permission on physical page ninety-eight continues onto ninety-nine to complete the close-enough-to-be-a-hazard qualifier. That complete exception is withheld as coverage debt rather than truncating its yielding condition.

The repeated intersection-look discussion spans physical pages ninety-nine and one hundred. The local repeated-scan instruction is covered; the full closing rationale and numeric travel-distance example are not represented as a complete one-page fact.

The passing-distance paragraph starts on physical page one hundred and continues onto one hundred one with the pavement-edge distance and emergency-space explanation. The complete paragraph requires a multi-page binding; the independently complete motorist passing-clearance rules on one hundred one are covered.

The first sharrow-purpose bullet begins on physical page one hundred one and completes on one hundred two with parked-door collision avoidance. The complete multi-page bullet is coverage debt; other complete purposes are locally sourced.

Sharrow and Bicycles May Use Full Lane visual recognition, and any other sharing-road illustrations in the mapped pages, have not received semantic image review. Text meanings are covered; image-based practice must wait.

Physical page one hundred six states that all hazardous-material vehicles stop at all railroad crossings. The following-driver preparedness rule is covered, but the universal legal classification and any statutory crossing or load exceptions require exact current official authority before being taught as universal.

self_reported_defects.what: Accepted wording says cancellation can follow false application information; source makes credential cancellation definite while perjury prosecution is possible.

self_reported_defects.proposed_statement: During the first six months of licensure, a driver younger than seventeen may carry at most one passenger younger than seventeen unless those passengers are related to the driver by blood, adoption or marriage.
